## 固定收益開場主論述

8月6日，美國公債各期限全面走跌。伊朗與阿曼針對荷莫茲海峽提出的方案內容有限，且爭議日益升高，扭轉前一交易日能源風險部分緩解的走勢；聯準會官員同時明確保留升息可能。2年期殖利率上升6.6個基點至4.249%，5年期上升7.1個基點至4.397%，10年期上升6.6個基點至4.681%，30年期則上升5.8個基點至5.227%。2年期與10年期走勢相近，使2s10s曲線維持43.2個基點不變；2s30s則趨平0.8個基點至97.8個基點。

這波賣壓幾乎平均來自通膨溢價與實質折現率上升。10年期實質殖利率上升3.5個基點至2.432%，10年期損益兩平通膨率則上升3.1個基點至2.249%。市場傳出伊朗與阿曼的安排可能限制美國、以色列及其他船舶通行，而非恢復海峽正常交通後，WTI原油上漲3.80%至$78.08。原本市場期待的重新開放，因條款細節而轉變為能源供應及通膨路徑的另一項不確定因素。

美國數據並未一致指向收緊政策。初領失業救濟人數維持低檔，生產力優於預期，單位勞動成本也低於市場共識；然而，續領失業救濟人數增幅超出預期，顯示失業者重新找到工作的能力仍偏弱。數據說明產出保持韌性未必會機械式地轉化為更快的勞動成本通膨，但就業也未出現足以明確排除再次升息的全面惡化。

較強的政策約束訊號來自聯準會官員談話。舊金山聯準銀行總裁Mary Daly支持7月按兵不動，但警告關稅、能源成本與人工智慧投資若共同擴散，可能需要迅速因應，而不是逐步收緊。7月主張升息25個基點的聖路易聯準銀行總裁Alberto Musalem表示，決策官員不能因期待未來的生產力紅利，就容忍當前通膨。據報導，主席Kevin Warsh若接下來的通膨數據偏高，準備在9月升息；但他提供的指引有限，市場仍不確定個別數據將如何轉化為政策決定。

因此，本交易日油價走強及市場對聯準會反應函數的疑慮，蓋過有利的生產力與勞動成本數據。跨市場呈現壓力，但未陷入失序。標普500指數下跌0.18%，Nasdaq 100下跌0.39%，美元指數上升0.26%；黃金期貨上漲1.72%至$4,318.80。投資級債券基金LQD下跌0.36%，長天期政府債與公司債指數的價格跌幅也大於較短天期債券。

## 油價與聯準會不確定性同步推升美債殖利率兩大組成

美債走勢逆轉前一交易日的穩定局面，但殖利率曲線的單日斜率並未明顯改變。5年期殖利率上升7.1個基點，為各期限之最，但僅略高於2年期與10年期。這種型態顯示市場同時重新評價近期政策約束與中期通膨展望，而非僅反映長端供給衝擊。30年期殖利率單日升幅較小，但仍高於5.2%；過去一個月累計上升24.2個基點，大於2年期的13.7個基點。

損益兩平通膨率再度上升，反映荷莫茲海峽情勢轉變。伊朗與阿曼一直在協商海峽航運管理方案，德黑蘭稱協議已進入最後階段。不過，伊朗外交部副部長Kazem Gharibabadi提醒，這項安排並不代表全面重啟通行，美國也不是協議參與方。伊朗媒體隨後報導，與美國、以色列及其他被視為敵對國家有關的船舶，可能遭拒絕通行或被要求支付補償。

這些條款削弱了協議可迅速使波斯灣能源運輸恢復正常的預期。細節傳出後，油價盤中一度上漲逾5%，WTI終場上漲3.80%。該期貨過去一週仍下跌6.59%，保留先前部分跌幅，但仍較一個月前上漲13.90%。胡塞武裝對葉門獲沙烏地阿拉伯支持的政府發動大規模攻擊，也增加衝突影響區域航運及能源風險的另一條途徑。

勞動市場數據同時提供聯準會耐心等待與保持警戒的理由。截至8月1日當週，初領失業救濟人數為19.9萬，低於20.2萬的市場共識，僅略高於前週修正後的19.8萬。Challenger公布7月企業裁員人數為33,429人，低於前值45,849人，也遠低於59,000人的預測。兩項數據均未顯示新增裁員突然升高。

續領失業救濟人數則較不令人安心。截至7月25日當週，續領人數由修正後的177.7萬增至180.1萬，高於179萬的市場共識。初領人數偏低、續領人數卻上升，顯示企業並未積極裁員，但已失業者重返職場所需時間變長。因此，7月就業報告中的聘僱廣度、勞參率及薪資廣度將更為重要，不能單憑申領失業救濟數據就認定勞動市場強勁。

生產力數據則改善了通膨平衡的供給面。第2季非農生產力初值以年率計成長1.4%，高於0.6%的市場共識及修正後的前值0.8%。單位勞動成本上升1.3%，與修正後的第1季增幅相同，但遠低於2.1%的市場共識。每小時產出成長加快、單位成本仍受抑制，意味經濟活動可以保持韌性，而不必伴隨同等幅度的勞動成本通膨。

6月批發庫存成長0.2%，低於預期及前月的0.3%，對經濟韌性構成小幅修正。這項數據不足以改寫成長全貌，但限制庫存累積對近期經濟活動的貢獻。

Daly以兩種通膨情境說明政策選擇。她認為較可能的結果仍是關稅、能源與AI相關價格壓力相對短暫，使聯準會得以維持利率不變；但另一種情境的風險正在增加，也就是這些力量相互疊加並向整體經濟擴散。若這種廣泛過程成形，她質疑僅採漸進式回應是否有效，並表示更迅速的行動可能較為適當。

Daly今年並非FOMC投票委員，而且完全支持7月將目標區間維持在3.5%至3.75%。因此，她傳遞的是條件式訊號，而非主張立即升息；關鍵在於未來數據究竟顯示個別衝擊逐漸消退，還是定價行為變得更廣泛、更持久。她也警告，長期通膨預期若進一步上升，決策官員將更難扭轉。

Musalem的立場更直接偏鷹。這位今年沒有投票權的聖路易聯準銀行總裁表示，他在7月會議主張升息25個基點，並認為政策必須對基礎通膨形成實質約束。他反對因AI未來可能提高生產力，就容忍當前通膨高於2%；在他看來，聯準會對投資與成長的貢獻應是維持穩定的價格環境，而非為尚未實現的生產力紅利容忍通膨。

Musalem認為，供給衝擊與AI帶動的需求都是通膨力量。他的良性情境以關稅效應消退及油價下降為前提；不利情境則是通膨停留在2.5%至3%或更高，因而需要略高的利率。他表示，月度通膨讀值略低於0.2%，才可證明物價漲幅正回到目標，這也為市場提供比Warsh更具體的判斷基準。

Warsh的政策取向仍是長天期債券的另一項風險來源。他減少前瞻指引，主張市場應自行因應最新資訊，不應依靠央行的詳細訊息引導。《金融時報》報導，即使7月會議後債市大幅下跌，他仍計畫維持這項策略；若通膨數據偏高，也準備在9月升息。

投資人的問題不只是缺少利率預測。Warsh很少解釋自己如何解讀特定數據，也未充分說明聯準會如何在維持利率與收緊政策之間取捨。結果是每項數據對市場的影響加大，政策後果卻依然不明。彭博美元即期指數的1日期權成本升至7月30日以來最高，1週波動率也在非農就業報告及隔週通膨數據公布前上升。

據報導，Donald Trump總統自Warsh出任主席以來不時致電，令不確定性增添制度層面。據稱Trump曾詢問Warsh的預測及看法，但沒有跡象顯示談話涉及利率指示。即便如此，在市場已經評估聯準會抗通膨可信度之際，這種聯繫仍偏離白宮與聯準會領導人通常保持的距離。

不確定性上升也反映在長端。彭博經濟研究估計，本週30年期美債期限溢價為1.56%，創2013年以來最高。部分投資人重新建立殖利率曲線陡峭化部位，理由是前端約束有限，加上聯準會指引稀少，使長天期債券承擔更多通膨、政策可信度及財政供給風險。

較廣泛的證據尚未顯示投資人不加區分地撤出美國資產。海外投資人在5月持有$9.4兆美國公債，較一年前增加4%。Pimco估計，今年同時出現美元下跌、10年期美債走跌及美國投資級信用利差擴大的單日與滾動5日區間，都只有約2%。8月6日債券下跌，但美元上漲，股票僅小幅走低。因此，本交易日提高了投資人承擔美國債券存續期間風險所要求的補償，卻未構成全面撤離美元資產的證據。

## 受限的荷莫茲方案收回部分能源利多

伊朗與阿曼的談判在程序上取得進展，但隨著條款浮現，經濟價值反而下降。德黑蘭稱，擬議路線是管理海上交通的機制，而非恢復不受限制的通行，並堅稱華府不在安排之內。Trump總統再度表示協議即將達成，但他先前對迅速取得突破的預測，並未帶來持久的通行條件。

市場最初把談判視為增加供給的途徑；但伊朗報導指出，美國與以色列船舶可能繼續遭禁，其他國家也可能面臨附加條件或補償要求，削弱了這項解讀。若限制持續，航運公司、保險業者及能源買家仍須逐一評估哪些船旗與貨物可以安全通行，海峽也就無法恢復正常商業運作。

影響並不限於原油。油價上漲之際，新興市場貨幣回吐漲幅，南非蘭特與匈牙利福林觸及盤中低點，巴西里爾及墨西哥披索也縮減升幅。能源進口國仍承受燃料成本上升的風險；若地緣政治衝擊尚未壓倒風險偏好，高收益、商品連動貨幣則仍可獲利差收益支撐。

美國市場當日對通膨的重新定價幅度明顯，但仍屬可控。10年期損益兩平通膨率上升3.1個基點，逆轉前一交易日跌幅，過去一個月則幾乎未變。這顯示，即使較長期通膨補償尚未明確突破上升，市場對近期能源情勢的評估仍可迅速改變。實質殖利率同時上升3.5個基點，也顯示能源並非美債賣壓的唯一來源；聯準會訊息、政策不確定性及投資人承擔存續期間風險所要求的報酬，都對債市不利。

儘管美元走強，黃金期貨仍上漲，過去一週累計升幅擴大至5.33%。即使原油在一週內數度改變短期方向，黃金表現仍反映市場對地緣政治與貨幣政策不確定性的避險需求。相較之下，股市在油價反彈時僅小幅下跌；VIX下降4.17%至15.15，顯示投資人並未將不完整的荷莫茲協議視為廣泛的市場危機。

## Alphabet完成巨額發債，AI債務市場選擇性升高

Alphabet發行$250億投資級債券，分為10個批次，期限涵蓋2年至40年，最高認購金額約$1,150億。這是今年AI相關借款人規模最大的訂單之一，僅次於Oracle在2月吸引的約$1,290億，以及Amazon在3月的約$1,260億；訂單也超過原先預期發行規模的4倍。

龐大需求顯示，投資人在7月市場下跌後並未退出AI融資，但定價也反映資金承接能力並非沒有代價。Alphabet提供的發行讓利高於平常；最長天期債券相對美國公債的利差，從最初討論的約155個基點收斂至130個基點完成定價。該公司2月發行的美元債券週四也走弱，交易利差已寬於發行時水準。

Alphabet還告知投資人，計畫每年發行兩次美元債。這項說明旨在提高融資規律的可預測性，但也確認反覆供給將持續成為信用市場的一部分。最新交易使Alphabet自2025年初以來的發債總額超過$1,140億，成為這段期間最大的AI相關債券發行人。

這筆借款緊隨計畫投資大幅增加。Alphabet把2026年資本支出展望調高至最多$2,050億，超過2025年支出的兩倍，並公布自2004年首次公開發行以來首度出現單季負現金流。公司2月已發行$200億美元債券，吸引約$1,030億認購，隨後又以瑞士法郎、英鎊、歐元、加幣及日圓發債。

新債進入市場時，供給已相當擁擠。Alphabet是週四8家投資級發行人之一，使當週發行量達$800億，為今年第三高。前一週，一家與BlackRock有關的借款人剛為Meta資料中心計畫發行$125億債券；Amazon及其他AI相關發行人則曾面臨需求轉弱或次級市場交易疲弱。

因此，Alphabet的結果說明，異常龐大的訂單簿可以與投資人保持審慎同時存在。只要債券提供足夠殖利率，買方仍願意沿殖利率曲線為高評等借款人提供資金，但既有債券也承受部分投資組合再平衡壓力。市場目前的考驗已不只是交易能否完成，而是反覆發債者須提供多少讓利，以及其流通在外債券能否在發行後回穩。

審慎態度也擴散至資料中心證券化。最近3筆為資料中心融資的商用不動產抵押貸款債券中，有2筆須較初步定價討論擴大利差才能吸引需求，包括與KKR支持的CyrusOne及Blackstone支持的QTS有關的交易。截至7月底，資料中心CMBS發行量約為$57億，占整體CMBS發行量7.3%。

整個產業的風險溢價均已上升。截至7月28日，單一借款人資料中心交易的AAA券利差由一年前高於SOFR 153個基點，擴大至168個基點；BBB-券利差則由321個基點升至332個基點。相較困境信用資產的重新定價，幅度仍不算大，但已顯示市場對AI槓桿及技術淘汰的疑慮，正從超大規模雲端業者的無擔保債券向外擴散。

在此情況下，交易結構的重要性提高。QTS最新CMBS期限為20年，但10年後即可選擇清償，類似資料中心資產擔保證券常見的軟性與硬性還款日期。較早再融資可以降低債務仍以過時技術為支撐的風險，但增加借款人的彈性，也可能降低流動性，並要求更高補償。

並非每筆交易都遇到困難。Blue Owl一筆規模較小的交易在6月依初步指引定價，擔保資產是維吉尼亞州一座出租給投資級超大規模雲端業者的資料中心。這項結果連同Alphabet的發債顯示，投資人是依槓桿、租戶品質、結構及價格加以區分，而非全面退出這項投資題材。投資人可以等待下一筆交易，也進一步提高其選擇性；JPMorgan估計，至2030年超大規模雲端業者將投入約$5.5兆建設AI基礎設施，其中很大一部分將以債務融資。

另一項資本事件則暴露房貸業的壓力。美國最大房貸業者United Wholesale Mortgage公布淨損$4.52億，並暫停上市以來一直支付的季度股利後，股價一度重挫49%。公司宣布將接受Oaktree Capital Management，以及執行長Mat Ishbia及其家族持有的投資工具合計$20.5億股權投資。

這項方案包括立即投入$16.5億，以及計畫中的$4億現金增資認股。Oaktree將取得基本年股利至少10%的特別股，初始金額相當於$1.5億。UWM可以把未付股利計入特別股本金，而非以現金支付；但贖回溢價會隨時間升高，最高可達60%。若7年後Oaktree仍持有至少25%的特別股，便可掌握董事會多數席次並推動清算。

UWM第2季虧損包括為收購Two Harbors失敗所建立的利率避險部位損失$6.03億。注資可強化近期流動性，但代價高昂的特別股條款，將可觀價值及控制權保障轉移給新投資人。這起事件再次說明，只要證券條件能補償資金提供者承擔的損失與公司治理風險，承壓的金融公司仍可取得信用融資。

## 日本標售獲得需求，但未動用聯準會備援工具

本週稍早10年期日本公債標售疲弱後，30年期標售獲得足以穩定超長端市場的需求。投標倍數為3.86倍，低於前次標售的4.55倍，但高於過去12個月平均的3.49倍。結果公布後，30年期殖利率下降6.5個基點至3.895%，20年期殖利率則下降5個基點至3.64%。

標售細節並非全面強勁。重新發行的4%票息公債平均殖利率為3.94%，低於前月，標售尾差則擴大；約24%的債券由單一買方取得。配置集中且投標倍數低於7月，使這次結果不足以證明需求廣泛，但接近4%的殖利率仍吸引到足以讓標售過關的支撐。

超長端市場的財政與貨幣政策風險仍彼此交織。首相高市早苗正推動長期投資計畫及增加國防支出，執政自民黨則通過暫時下調食品消費稅兩年的方案，卻尚未決定財源。日本央行總裁植田和男保留9月升息的可能後，市場同時賦予該月升息約62%的機率。

國際貨幣基金也支持持續推進政策正常化。第一副總裁Dan Katz表示，日本經濟轉型，加上通膨略高於目標，使日本央行有空間進一步擺脫維持數十年的異常低利率。這項評估與先前政策調整對短天期債券造成的壓力一致；另一方面，標售也顯示長債殖利率達到一定絕對水準後可以吸引買方。

聯準會最新數據釐清了日本近期外匯操作的部分融資方式。截至8月5日當週，外國及國際貨幣當局附買回機制（FIMA）餘額仍為零，已連續第8週未被使用。因此，日本在首日估計約¥8.45兆、即$530億，以及次日約¥5.33兆、即$340億的操作中，並未依賴這項機制。

FIMA允許外國貨幣當局質押美國公債籌措美元，而不必出售債券，每一交易對手每日額度為$600億。其定價具有備援工具性質：隔夜融資成本為聯準會目標區間上緣，目前是3.75%；1週融資成本則為隔夜指數交換利率加25個基點。最新數據顯示日本未使用FIMA，排除了市場對干預融資途徑的一項即時疑慮，卻未揭示實際採用的替代方式。

聯準會外國官方附買回池餘額當週減少約$170億至$3,180億，兩週合計減少近$350億。由於數據沒有辨識提款機構，因此無法證明這就是日本的資金來源。外國政府也可先累積利息收入、等待美國國庫券及附息債到期，或動用存款，而不必出售較長天期證券。

日本國內信用市場也同步適應較高的主權債殖利率。第一生命已接觸數十家很少或從未發債的公司，並提議擔任核心買方。自該保險公司於2025年4月啟動這項計畫以來，已有4家接觸對象發債，其中兩家為首次發行。截至3月底，第一生命在¥33.9兆投資組合中持有約¥1.8兆日圓公司債。

這項計畫部分鎖定BBB評等及無評等公司。日本國內公司債中，98%評等為A級以上，BBB級僅占2%。日圓殖利率升高，加上避險美元資產的成本上升，使國內公司債對負債以日圓計價的保險公司更具競爭力。

隨著借款人範圍擴大，投資人保障也正在增加。2026年前7個月，日本企業發行附契約條款債券共¥468億，已超過2025年全年的¥446億。許多債券納入控制權變更條款，允許公司遭收購後提前償還。相較日本高評等債市，這項成長規模仍小，但顯示利率升高正吸引新發行人轉向債券融資，投資人也要求更多保障，以因應槓桿、下市及降評風險。

## 通膨風險使全球政策路徑持續分歧

墨西哥央行連續第二次會議一致決議將政策利率維持在6.50%，並重申維持現行利率是適當做法。受訪的28位經濟學家全都預期這項決定，但隨附的通膨預測降低了2026年重新降息的可能性。

7月上半月整體通膨由6月上半月的3.18%及3月中旬的4.63%，放緩至3.1%，已接近墨西哥央行3%的目標。然而，服務通膨仍為4.36%，央行並把預期通膨回到目標的時間由2027年第2季延後至第4季，也繼續將伊朗戰爭列為上行風險。

聲明公布後，利率交換上升，2年期合約上升5個基點至6.72%，披索則維持在約17.20兌1美元。墨西哥央行指出第2季經濟復甦更為穩健，並維持全年1.1%的成長預測。經濟活動改善、服務價格僵固及通膨收斂日期延後的組合，使央行幾乎沒有立即恢復降息的壓力。

哥倫比亞的內部辯論方向則與討論寬鬆相反。央行共同理事Mauricio Villamizar警告，不應把7月31日的暫停升息解讀為鴿派訊號。決策官員以4比3表決將利率維持在12%，Villamizar則支持升息50個基點。他認為，及早升息的成本會低於延後行動後再逐步收緊。

Villamizar判斷，目前的限制性政策仍不足以在2027年底前把通膨降至4%以下，也就是目標區間上緣。在擴張性財政政策、薪資漲幅超越生產力成長、伊朗衝擊及聖嬰現象風險下，通膨預計將在2026年底接近7%，明年仍高於4%。2年期利率交換部分收回先前跌幅，投資人持續反映收緊週期可能尚未結束。

他也否認央行計畫透過賣權累積最多$40億外匯存底，是為了壓低披索。今年披索兌美元已升值近20%，受到利差收益及市場預期候任總統Abelardo de la Espriella將強化財政紀律支持。Villamizar表示，哥倫比亞失去國際貨幣基金彈性信用額度後，外匯存底適足性指標轉弱，才是這項計畫的原因。

俄羅斯則呈現更偏制度面的利率不確定性。長期公開捍衛央行獨立性的總統Vladimir Putin，7月兩度表示基準利率應該調低，屬於罕見干預。俄羅斯央行隨後將政策利率調降25個基點至14%，延續寬鬆循環，但未提供央行總裁Elvira Nabiullina任內一向重視的前瞻指引。

央行表示決定仍由自身作出，並重申4%的通膨目標不變，政策將致力於在2027年達標。然而，周邊數據使降息充滿爭議。官員把年底通膨預測由4.5%至5.5%上調至6%至7%，將2026年成長預測由0.5%至1.5%下修至0%至1%，通膨預期也升至2022年以來最高。即使汽油價格單週下跌，一度使經濟陷入輕微通縮，年通膨仍加速至6.11%。

會議紀錄顯示，鴿派僅以些微優勢勝出。決策官員普遍認為煉油廠造成的燃料衝擊是暫時現象，但對家庭會繼續審慎消費，還是加快支出以保護儲蓄價值意見不一。官員較重視企業對未來需求預期轉弱；反對者則認為，沒有足夠證據顯示較強的消費需求與價格壓力將會消退。

因此，俄羅斯下次決策考驗的不只是通膨預測。市場將觀察央行對煉油產能恢復及需求放緩的假設，能否承受進一步干擾，也要判斷更廣泛的降低信貸成本政治訴求是否改變政策路徑。央行的正式目標仍然存在，但省略指引及總統公開發言已降低政策能見度。

印度形成區域內另一項對照。印度央行決定將利率維持在5.25%後，交換利率下移，交易員把預期首次升息時間由10月延後至12月。市場反映未來一年約升息50個基點，低於會議前約75個基點。Goldman Sachs也把預期首次升息時間延至12月，並表示核心通膨較弱，可能使啟動時間進一步延後至2027年2月。

這項重新定價的基礎，是通膨仍在印度央行2%至6%的區間內，而且幾乎沒有證據顯示價格壓力正從燃料及其他供給衝擊向外擴散。總裁Sanjay Malhotra以汽車銷售、採購經理人調查及銀行信貸穩健為由，把截至2027年3月止年度的成長預測由6.6%上調至6.7%。即將到來的節慶消費季，將檢驗消費增強能否與基礎物價壓力受控並存。

菲律賓債市面臨通膨偏高與供給增加的更困難組合。10年期殖利率接近7.25%；7月殖利率上升52個基點，當月本地債券報酬率為-1.74%。菲律賓聯合銀行預期殖利率將升至7.60%至7.80%，Aberdeen Investments則預估落在7.20%至7.60%。7月通膨維持6.2%，超過3%目標的兩倍後，投資人繼續反映菲律賓央行8月27日會議升息25個基點。

較高殖利率最終可能吸引國內需求；Maybank預期，殖利率高於7.50%後將出現較明顯買盤。不過，政府發債時程偏重後段，加上到期量有限，可能抵銷這項支撐。因此，能吸引投資人的殖利率水準，也正是市場在必須消化另一次升息與額外供給時可能抵達的區間。

捷克央行一如預期將利率維持在3.75%，延續其偏向收緊的立場，與中歐部分國家預期寬鬆形成對照。另一方面，阿根廷與中國人民銀行續簽約$190億貨幣交換協議，期限為5年，確保外匯存底備援延續至2027年總統大選。

## 後續市場意義

8月7日公布的美國7月就業報告，是檢驗本輪美債賣壓，以及聯準會在官員立場分歧下將如何反應的首要事件。市場預期非農就業增加8萬人，前值為5.7萬人，失業率則維持4.2%不變。聘僱廣度、薪資及勞參率須釐清：偏低的初領失業救濟人數究竟代表勞動市場仍具韌性，還是續領人數增加更能反映再就業能力轉弱。

強勁報告將支持Musalem要求政策發揮實質約束作用的主張，也會提高Daly所說廣泛通膨情境的相關性。疲弱結果則將提供聯準會更多等待理由，尤其第2季生產力優於預期、單位勞動成本增幅又低於預測。之後公布的通膨數據，須對照Musalem提出的基準評估：月增幅略低於0.2%，才支持通膨回到2%。

荷莫茲海峽需要的是實際恢復通行，而非另一項外交里程碑。關鍵問題包括哪些船舶可使用擬議路線、美國及其他遭排除國家是否接受安排、保險業者是否認定通行安全，以及攻擊是否擴散至替代航道。若航線能恢復持續的商業交通，能源對損益兩平通膨率的推升作用將減弱；限制、補償要求或攻擊再起，則會維持通膨溢價。

Alphabet新債是AI融資承接能力的下一項考驗。大額訂單完成配置後，次級市場交易將顯示最長天期債券130個基點的利差，以及整體發行讓利，是否足以支撐交易。若新債與Alphabet的2月債券都能穩定，將可區分對價格敏感的真實需求與暫時膨脹的訂單；若利差進一步擴大，則更能證明即使初級市場交易可以完成，超大規模雲端業者反覆發債仍在占用更多機構承接能力。

日本9月政策預期仍同時取決於國內通膨及日圓。30年期標售顯示，接近4%的殖利率可以吸引需求，但尾差擴大、配置集中，仍不足以證明超長期債券獲得廣泛支持。下一次外匯干預還將揭示，日本是否繼續避開FIMA、改由外國官方現金池籌資，或開始使用其曾表示未來操作可能採用的聯準會備援工具。

全球收緊政策的考驗仍因國而異。俄羅斯9月會議須判斷，在通膨預測上升及政治力量要求降低利率的情況下，央行是否仍認定燃料價格壓力只是暫時現象。菲律賓8月27日的決策，將檢驗再度升息是否把10年期殖利率推向策略師預期買盤增強的區域。在印度，秋季消費旺季與下一批核心通膨數據，將決定市場把首次升息預期延後至12月的定價能否持續。

overall_summary.headline: 受限的荷莫茲方案重燃油價風險，聯準會官員保留升息可能，美債全面走跌
overall_summary.session_narrative:
伊朗與阿曼航運方案浮現的條款顯示，美國、以色列及其他船舶通過荷莫茲海峽仍可能受限，帶動美國公債各期限殖利率上升。WTI上漲3.80%至$78.08，推動10年期損益兩平通膨率上升3.1個基點至2.249%；10年期實質殖利率也上升3.5個基點至2.432%。名目10年期殖利率上升6.6個基點至4.681%，2年期與10年期升幅相近，使2s10s曲線維持43.2個基點不變。

美國數據提供耐心等待的理由，但未釐清政策前景。生產力優於預期，單位勞動成本低於市場共識；偏低的初領失業救濟人數則與較高的續領人數形成對照。聯準會官員仍強調，關稅、能源成本及AI投資可能使通膨壓力擴散；據報導，主席Kevin Warsh若通膨偏高，準備在9月升息。

信用市場仍可提供資金，但對價格愈來愈敏感。Alphabet發行$250億債券，最高認購金額約$1,150億，但在投資人評估AI相關供給反覆增加之際，公司仍須提供較大讓利。跨市場呈現壓力而非失序，股市小幅下跌、美元走強，波動率則下降。
overall_summary.summary: 油價上升推高通膨補償，市場對聯準會反應函數的不確定性則推升實質殖利率，兩者蓋過有利的生產力及勞動成本數據，使10年期殖利率上升6.6個基點至4.681%。

section_summaries.summary: 油價走強及市場對聯準會如何因應通膨的不確定性，蓋過有利的生產力與勞動成本數據。實質殖利率和損益兩平通膨率升幅幾乎相等，帶動名目美債殖利率上揚。殖利率曲線變化不大，股市僅小幅下跌、美元走強，顯示市場承壓，但並未全面撤離美國資產。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries sold off across maturities on Aug. 6 as a partial and increasingly contested plan for the Strait of Hormuz reversed some of the previous session’s energy relief, while Federal Reserve officials kept the possibility of higher rates firmly in view. The 2-year yield rose 6.6 basis points to 4.249%, the 5-year climbed 7.1 basis points to 4.397%, the 10-year increased 6.6 basis points to 4.681% and the 30-year added 5.8 basis points to 5.227%. The similar moves at 2 and 10 years left the 2s10s curve unchanged at 43.2 basis points, while 2s30s flattened 0.8 basis point to 97.8 basis points.

The selloff divided almost evenly between a higher inflation premium and a higher real discount rate. The 10-year real yield rose 3.5 basis points to 2.432%, while the 10-year breakeven increased 3.1 basis points to 2.249%. WTI crude gained 3.80% to $78.08 after reports that an Iran-Oman arrangement could restrict passage by US, Israeli and other vessels rather than restore normal traffic through the strait. The details turned an anticipated reopening into another source of uncertainty about energy supply and the inflation path.

US data did not point uniformly toward tighter policy. Initial jobless claims remained low, productivity exceeded expectations and unit labor costs undershot consensus. Continuing claims nevertheless rose more than forecast, preserving a softer signal about workers’ ability to find new jobs. The releases suggested that resilient output need not translate mechanically into faster labor-cost inflation, but they did not provide the broad deterioration in employment that would make another rate increase clearly unnecessary.

Fed communication supplied the stronger restraint. San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly supported the July hold but warned that a broadening combination of tariffs, energy costs and artificial-intelligence investment could require a rapid response rather than incremental tightening. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem, who preferred a quarter-point increase in July, said policymakers could not tolerate current inflation in anticipation of a future productivity dividend. Chair Kevin Warsh was reported to be prepared to raise rates in September if coming inflation data run hot, even as his limited guidance continues to leave markets uncertain about how individual releases map into policy.

The result was a session in which firmer oil and doubts about the Fed’s reaction function outweighed favorable productivity and labor-cost figures. Cross-markets showed pressure rather than disorder. The S&P 500 fell 0.18% and the Nasdaq 100 declined 0.39%, while the dollar index rose 0.26%. Gold futures gained 1.72% to $4,318.80. Investment-grade bond fund LQD lost 0.36%, and long-maturity government and corporate bond indices posted larger price declines than shorter-duration debt.

## Oil and Fed Uncertainty Lift Both Components of Treasury Yields

The Treasury move reversed the stability of the previous close without materially changing the curve’s daily slope. The 5-year sector registered the largest yield increase at 7.1 basis points, only slightly more than the 2- and 10-year moves. That pattern was consistent with a repricing of both near-term policy restraint and the medium-term inflation outlook, rather than a long-end-only supply shock. The 30-year yield rose less on the day but remained above 5.2%, and its 24.2-basis-point increase over one month was larger than the 13.7-basis-point rise at 2 years.

The renewed rise in breakevens reflected the change in the Hormuz story. Iran and Oman had been negotiating a plan to manage shipping through the strait, and Tehran said an agreement was in its final stages. Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi cautioned that the arrangement would not constitute a full reopening and that the US was not a party to it. Iranian media subsequently reported that vessels associated with the US, Israel and other countries considered hostile could be denied passage or required to pay compensation.

Those terms weakened the premise that an agreement would quickly normalize Gulf energy flows. Oil rose more than 5% at one point as the details circulated, before WTI finished with a 3.80% gain. The contract was still 6.59% lower over one week, preserving some of the earlier relief, but it stood 13.90% higher than one month earlier. A large-scale Houthi attack against Yemen’s Saudi-backed government added another route through which the conflict could affect regional shipping and energy risk.

The labor releases gave the Fed reasons for both patience and vigilance. Initial unemployment claims totaled 199,000 in the week through Aug. 1, below the 202,000 consensus and only slightly above the revised 198,000 reading in the prior week. Challenger reported 33,429 announced job cuts in July, down from 45,849 and far below the 59,000 forecast. Together, those figures offered little evidence of a sudden rise in new layoffs.

Continuing claims were less reassuring. They increased to 1.801 million in the week through July 25 from a revised 1.777 million, exceeding the 1.790 million consensus. The contrast between low initial claims and rising continuing claims suggested that companies were not dismissing workers aggressively, but that those already unemployed were taking longer to return to work. That distinction raises the importance of hiring, participation and wage breadth in the July employment report rather than making the claims data a simple signal of labor strength.

The productivity figures improved the supply side of the inflation balance. Preliminary Q2 nonfarm productivity rose at a 1.4% annualized rate, above the 0.6% consensus and the revised 0.8% prior reading. Unit labor costs increased 1.3%, matching the revised Q1 pace but falling well short of the 2.1% consensus. Faster output per hour alongside restrained unit costs offers a path by which activity can remain resilient without an equivalent increase in labor-driven inflation.

Wholesale inventories provided a modest qualification to that resilience, rising 0.2% in June rather than the 0.3% expected and recorded in the prior month. The figure was not large enough to redefine the growth picture, but it limited the contribution that inventory accumulation could make to near-term activity.

Daly’s remarks framed the policy implications as a choice between two inflation regimes. She said the more likely outcome remained one in which tariff, energy and AI-related price pressures prove relatively short-lived, allowing the Fed to hold rates. She nevertheless judged the risk of a second outcome—one in which those forces compound and spread across the economy—to be increasing. If that broader process takes hold, she questioned the value of responding only incrementally and indicated that moving rapidly could be more appropriate.

Daly is not an FOMC voter this year, and she fully supported the July decision to retain the 3.5%-to-3.75% target range. Her signal was therefore conditional rather than a call for an immediate increase. The condition is whether the coming data show isolated shocks fading or broader and more persistent price-setting behavior. She also warned that a further rise in long-term inflation expectations would be harder for policymakers to reverse.

Musalem’s position was more immediately hawkish. The nonvoting St. Louis Fed president said he had favored a 25-basis-point increase at the July meeting and argued that policy must impose meaningful restraint on underlying inflation. He rejected the idea that officials should accept inflation above 2% today because AI might eventually increase productivity, reasoning that the Fed’s contribution to investment and growth is a stable price backdrop rather than tolerance of a prospective productivity windfall.

Musalem identified both supply shocks and AI-driven demand as inflationary forces. His benign scenario requires fading tariff effects and lower oil prices. In the adverse case, inflation settles around 2.5% to 3% or higher and requires somewhat higher interest rates. He said monthly inflation readings slightly below 0.2% would provide evidence that price growth was returning toward target, giving markets a more specific benchmark than Warsh has supplied.

Warsh’s approach remains a separate source of duration risk. The chair has curtailed forward guidance and argued that markets should respond to incoming information without being steered by detailed central-bank messaging. The Financial Times reported that he plans to retain that strategy despite the sharp bond selloff following the July meeting and would be prepared to raise rates in September if inflation data are hot.

The problem for investors is not merely the absence of a rate forecast. Warsh has offered limited explanation of how he interprets particular data or how the Fed will choose between holding and tightening. That makes each release more powerful while leaving its policy consequence uncertain. One-day options on the Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index rose to their highest cost since July 30, and one-week volatility increased ahead of payrolls and the following week’s inflation data.

Reports that President Donald Trump has periodically called Warsh since he became chair added an institutional dimension. Trump was said to have asked about Warsh’s forecasts and opinions, although there was no indication that the conversations included interest-rate instructions. The contact nevertheless departed from the distance usually maintained between the White House and Fed leadership at a time when markets are already assessing the credibility of the inflation response.

The increase in uncertainty is visible at the long end. Bloomberg Economics estimated the term premium on the 30-year Treasury at 1.56% this week, its highest since 2013. Some investors have revived steepener positions on the view that modest restraint at the front end and sparse Fed guidance leave longer maturities carrying more inflation, credibility and fiscal-supply risk.

The broader evidence does not yet show an indiscriminate rejection of US assets. Foreign investors held $9.4 trillion of Treasuries in May, 4% more than a year earlier. Pimco estimated that only about 2% of trading days and rolling five-day periods this year produced simultaneous selloffs in the dollar, 10-year Treasuries and US investment-grade credit spreads. On Aug. 6, the dollar rose and equities slipped only modestly even as bonds declined. The session therefore added to the compensation demanded for US duration without establishing a generalized exit from dollar assets.

## A Restricted Hormuz Plan Reverses Part of the Energy Relief

The Iran-Oman negotiations moved forward procedurally but became less valuable economically as their terms emerged. Tehran described the proposed route as a mechanism for managing maritime traffic rather than a restoration of unrestricted passage. It also insisted that Washington was outside the arrangement. President Trump again said a deal was imminent, but earlier predictions of a rapid breakthrough had not produced durable access.

The market initially treated the negotiations as a path toward greater supply. That interpretation weakened when Iranian reports indicated that US and Israeli vessels could remain barred and that other countries could face conditions or compensation demands. Such restrictions would leave shipping companies, insurers and energy buyers assessing which flags and cargoes could move safely, rather than returning the strait to normal commercial operation.

The shift was visible beyond crude. Emerging-market currencies surrendered gains as oil rose, with the South African rand and Hungarian forint reaching their session lows. The Brazilian real and Mexican peso also trimmed advances. Importers remain exposed to higher fuel costs, while high-yielding commodity-linked currencies retain support from carry when the geopolitical shock does not overwhelm risk appetite.

The day’s US inflation repricing was meaningful but controlled. The 10-year breakeven rose 3.1 basis points, reversing the prior session’s decline, while remaining almost unchanged over one month. That combination showed how quickly the market’s near-term energy assessment could change even though longer-horizon inflation compensation had not broken decisively higher. The 3.5-basis-point increase in the real yield demonstrated that energy was not the only force: Fed communication, policy uncertainty and the required return on duration also moved against bonds.

Gold futures rose despite a firmer dollar, extending their one-week gain to 5.33%. The metal’s performance preserved demand for protection against geopolitical and monetary-policy uncertainty even as the immediate direction of crude changed several times during the week. Equities, by contrast, absorbed the oil rebound with relatively small index declines. The VIX fell 4.17% to 15.15, indicating that investors did not treat the incomplete Hormuz agreement as a broad market crisis.

## Alphabet Clears a Jumbo Sale as AI Debt Becomes More Selective

Alphabet sold $25 billion of investment-grade bonds across 10 tranches ranging from 2 to 40 years, attracting about $115 billion of peak orders. The book was among the largest for an AI-related borrower this year, behind the roughly $129 billion drawn by Oracle in February and approximately $126 billion for Amazon in March. It also exceeded four times the anticipated deal size.

The demand demonstrated that investors had not withdrawn from AI financing after July’s selloff, but the pricing showed that capacity came at a cost. Alphabet offered larger concessions than usual, and the longest maturity priced at a spread of 130 basis points over Treasuries after initial discussions around 155 basis points. Its February dollar bonds weakened during Thursday’s session and were trading wider than their issue levels.

Alphabet also told investors that it intends to issue US debt twice a year. That disclosure was meant to make its funding pattern more predictable, but it confirmed that repeated supply will remain part of the credit landscape. The latest deal lifted Alphabet’s debt issuance since the beginning of 2025 above $114 billion, making it the largest seller of AI-related bonds over that period.

The borrowing follows a sharp increase in planned investment. Alphabet raised its 2026 capital-spending outlook to as much as $205 billion, more than twice its 2025 expenditure, and reported its first quarter of negative cash flow since its 2004 initial public offering. It had already sold $20 billion of dollar bonds in February, attracting roughly $103 billion of orders, before issuing in Swiss francs, sterling, euros, Canadian dollars and yen.

The transaction arrived into a crowded market. Alphabet was one of eight investment-grade issuers on Thursday, bringing weekly volume to $80 billion, the third-highest total of the year. A BlackRock-linked borrower had sold $12.5 billion of bonds for a Meta data-center project the previous week, and Amazon and other AI-linked issuers had encountered softer demand or weaker secondary trading.

The Alphabet outcome therefore showed that an exceptionally large orderbook and investor caution can coexist. Buyers were willing to fund a highly rated borrower across the curve when the bonds provided sufficient yield, while existing paper absorbed some of the portfolio rebalancing. The test for the market is no longer simply whether a transaction can be completed, but how much concession recurring issuers must pay and whether their outstanding bonds stabilize afterward.

Caution is spreading into data-center securitization. Two of the three most recent commercial mortgage bond sales funding data centers widened from initial price discussions to attract demand, including deals associated with KKR-backed CyrusOne and Blackstone-backed QTS. Data-center CMBS issuance totaled about $5.7 billion through late July and represented 7.3% of overall CMBS issuance.

Risk premiums have increased across the sector. AAA portions of single-borrower data-center transactions widened to 168 basis points over SOFR as of July 28 from 153 basis points a year earlier. BBB- spreads increased to 332 basis points from 321 basis points. The moves were modest compared with a distressed-credit repricing, but they showed that concern about AI leverage and technological obsolescence was reaching beyond the unsecured bonds of hyperscalers.

Structure is becoming more important as a result. QTS’s latest CMBS has a 20-year maturity with an option to repay after 10 years, resembling the soft and hard repayment dates often used in data-center asset-backed securities. Earlier refinancing can reduce the risk that debt remains outstanding against obsolete technology, but added borrower flexibility can also reduce liquidity and require more compensation.

Not every deal has struggled. A smaller Blue Owl transaction in June priced in line with initial guidance and was backed by a Virginia data center leased to an investment-grade hyperscaler. That result, alongside Alphabet’s sale, suggests that investors are differentiating by leverage, tenant quality, structure and price rather than withdrawing from the theme altogether. The ability to wait for the next deal is increasing that selectivity: JPMorgan estimates that hyperscalers will spend about $5.5 trillion on AI infrastructure through 2030, much of it debt-financed.

A separate capital event exposed stress in mortgage lending. United Wholesale Mortgage shares fell as much as 49% after the largest US mortgage lender reported a $452 million net loss and suspended the quarterly dividend it had paid since going public. The company announced a $2.05 billion equity investment from Oaktree Capital Management and an investment vehicle owned by Chief Executive Officer Mat Ishbia and his family.

The package includes $1.65 billion immediately and a planned $400 million rights offering. Oaktree will receive preferred shares with a base annual dividend of at least 10%, equal initially to $150 million. UWM may add unpaid dividends to the preferred principal rather than pay cash, but redemptions carry a premium that rises over time to as much as 60%. If Oaktree retains at least 25% of its preferred shares after seven years, it can take a board majority and pursue liquidation.

UWM’s Q2 loss included $603 million on interest-rate hedges established for its failed attempt to acquire Two Harbors. The capital infusion strengthens near-term liquidity, but its expensive preferred terms transfer substantial value and control protection to the new investor. The episode was a reminder that credit access remains available to stressed financial companies when the security package compensates providers for loss and governance risk.

## Japan Finds Auction Demand but Does Not Use the Fed Backstop

Japan’s 30-year government-bond auction drew enough demand to calm the super-long sector after a weak 10-year sale earlier in the week. The bid-to-cover ratio was 3.86, below the previous auction’s 4.55 but above the 12-month average of 3.49. The 30-year yield fell 6.5 basis points after the result to 3.895%, while the 20-year yield declined 5 basis points to 3.64%.

The details were not uniformly strong. The reopened 4% bond produced an average yield of 3.94%, below the previous month, and the auction tail widened. About 24% of the bonds went to a single buyer. That concentration and the lower bid-to-cover ratio than in July kept the result from demonstrating broad demand, but yields near 4% were sufficient to attract a passing level of support.

Fiscal and monetary risks remain intertwined in the super-long sector. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is pursuing a long-term investment program and higher defense spending, while the ruling Liberal Democratic Party approved a temporary 2-year reduction in the sales tax on food without settling how it will be financed. At the same time, markets assigned about a 62% probability to a September Bank of Japan increase after Governor Kazuo Ueda kept that possibility alive.

The IMF added support for continued normalization. First Deputy Managing Director Dan Katz said Japan’s economic transformation and inflation modestly above target gave the BOJ room to move farther away from the exceptionally low rates maintained for decades. That assessment aligned with the pressure on shorter maturities from an earlier policy move, even as the auction showed that outright yield levels could draw buyers into long bonds.

New Fed data clarified how Japan financed its recent currency operations. The Foreign and International Monetary Authorities Repo Facility recorded no balances in the week through Aug. 5, its eighth consecutive week without use. Japan therefore did not rely on that facility for the operations estimated at about ¥8.45 trillion, or $53 billion, on the first day and ¥5.33 trillion, or $34 billion, on the second.

FIMA allows foreign monetary authorities to raise dollars by pledging Treasuries rather than selling them, subject to a $60 billion daily counterparty limit. It is priced as a backstop—overnight funding costs the top of the Fed’s target range, currently 3.75%, and 1-week funding costs the overnight-indexed swap rate plus 25 basis points. Its absence from the latest data resolves one immediate concern about the intervention’s funding route without identifying the alternative Japan used.

Foreign official balances in the Fed’s reverse-repurchase pool fell by about $17 billion during the week to $318 billion and by almost $35 billion over two weeks. The data do not identify the withdrawing authorities, so they cannot establish Japan’s funding source. Foreign governments can also accumulate interest payments, allow Treasury bills and coupons to mature or use deposits before selling longer-dated securities.

Japan’s domestic credit market is simultaneously adapting to higher sovereign yields. Daiichi Life has approached dozens of companies that have rarely or never issued bonds, offering to serve as a core buyer. Since the insurer began the initiative in April 2025, four targeted companies have issued debt, including two first-time borrowers. Daiichi held about ¥1.8 trillion of yen corporate bonds at the end of March within a ¥33.9 trillion portfolio.

The effort is aimed partly at BBB-rated and unrated companies in a market where 98% of domestic corporate bonds carry ratings of A or higher and only 2% are rated BBB. Higher yen yields and the cost of hedging dollar assets have made domestic corporate debt more competitive for insurers whose liabilities are denominated in yen.

Investor protections are expanding with the borrower base. Japanese companies sold ¥46.8 billion of bonds with covenants in the first seven months of 2026, already exceeding the ¥44.6 billion issued in all of 2025. Many include change-of-control clauses permitting early repayment after a takeover. The growth remains small relative to Japan’s high-grade market, but it shows higher rates drawing new issuers toward bonds while investors demand more protection from leverage, delisting and downgrade risk.

## Inflation Risk Keeps Global Policy Paths Divergent

Banxico unanimously held its policy rate at 6.50% for a second consecutive meeting and repeated that maintaining the current rate would be appropriate. The decision was expected by all 28 economists surveyed, but the accompanying inflation forecast reduced the prospect of renewed easing in 2026.

Headline inflation slowed to 3.1% in the first half of July from 3.18% in the first half of June and 4.63% in mid-March. That brought it close to Banxico’s 3% target. Services inflation remained at 4.36%, however, and the bank moved its expected return to target to Q4 2027 from Q2 2027. It also retained the Iran war as an upside risk.

Interest-rate swaps rose after the announcement, with 2-year contracts increasing 5 basis points to 6.72%, while the peso held around 17.20 per dollar. Banxico’s statement described a firmer Q2 reactivation and retained a 1.1% growth forecast for the year. That combination—better activity, sticky services prices and a delayed inflation convergence date—left little pressure for an immediate resumption of cuts.

Colombia’s internal debate moved in the opposite direction from an easing discussion. Central-bank co-director Mauricio Villamizar warned against interpreting the July 31 pause as dovish. Policymakers held the rate at 12% in a 4-3 vote, with Villamizar supporting a 50-basis-point increase. He argued that raising rates sooner would be less costly than delaying and then tightening gradually.

Villamizar judged the current restrictive stance insufficient to return inflation below 4%, the top of the target range, by the end of 2027. Inflation is projected to finish 2026 near 7% and remain above 4% next year amid expansionary fiscal policy, wage increases beyond productivity growth, the Iran shock and El Niño risk. Two-year swaps partly reversed their earlier decline as investors continued to price the possibility that tightening was not finished.

He also rejected the interpretation that the central bank’s plan to accumulate as much as $4 billion of reserves through put options was intended to weaken the peso. The currency has appreciated almost 20% against the dollar this year, supported by carry and expectations of stronger fiscal discipline under President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella. Villamizar linked the reserve plan instead to weaker adequacy indicators after Colombia lost access to the IMF’s Flexible Credit Line.

Russia supplied a more institutional form of rate uncertainty. President Vladimir Putin twice indicated in July that the key rate should be lower, an unusual intervention from a leader who had long publicly defended central-bank independence. The Bank of Russia subsequently cut its policy rate by 25 basis points to 14%, extending its easing cycle without the forward guidance that had been a feature of Governor Elvira Nabiullina’s tenure.

The central bank said the decision remained its own and reiterated that the 4% inflation target was unchanged, with policy aimed at reaching it in 2027. The surrounding data nevertheless made the reduction contentious. Officials raised their year-end inflation forecast to 6%-7% from 4.5%-5.5%, cut their 2026 growth projection to 0%-1% from 0.5%-1.5%, and faced inflation expectations at their highest since 2022. Annual inflation accelerated to 6.11% even as a weekly decline in gasoline prices briefly pushed the economy into marginal deflation.

Accounts of the meeting indicated that the doves prevailed narrowly. Policymakers broadly viewed the refinery-driven fuel shock as temporary, but disagreed over whether households would remain cautious or accelerate spending to protect savings. Officials gave greater weight to weaker business expectations for future demand, while opponents said there was not enough evidence that stronger consumer demand and price pressure would fade.

The next Russian decision will therefore test more than the inflation forecast. It will show whether the bank’s assumption that refinery capacity will recover and demand will moderate can withstand further disruption, and whether the broader political campaign for cheaper credit changes the policy path. The institution’s formal target remains intact, but the omission of guidance and the president’s public comments have reduced visibility.

India continued to provide a regional contrast. Following the Reserve Bank of India’s decision to hold at 5.25%, swaps shifted lower and traders moved the expected first increase to December from October. Markets priced about 50 basis points of tightening over the next year, down from roughly 75 basis points before the meeting. Goldman Sachs also moved its expected first increase to December and said weaker core inflation could defer the start to February 2027.

The repricing rested on inflation remaining within the RBI’s 2%-to-6% band and showing limited evidence of broadening beyond fuel and other supply shocks. Governor Sanjay Malhotra raised the growth forecast for the year through March 2027 to 6.7% from 6.6%, citing firm automobile sales, purchasing-managers’ surveys and bank credit. The coming festive season will test whether stronger consumption can coexist with contained underlying prices.

Philippine bonds face the more difficult combination of elevated inflation and supply. The 10-year yield was near 7.25% after rising 52 basis points in July, when local bonds returned negative 1.74%. Union Bank of the Philippines expects the yield to reach 7.60%-7.80%, while Aberdeen Investments sees a 7.20%-7.60% range. Investors continued to price a 25-basis-point increase at the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas’ Aug. 27 meeting after July inflation remained at 6.2%, more than twice the 3% target.

Higher yields could eventually attract domestic demand: Maybank expects meaningful buying above 7.50%. Back-loaded government issuance and light maturities may counter that support, however. The level that attracts investors is therefore also the area the market may reach if another policy increase and additional supply must be absorbed.

The Czech National Bank held its rate at 3.75% as expected, preserving the contrast between its tightening bias and anticipated easing in parts of Central Europe. Argentina, meanwhile, renewed an approximately $19 billion currency swap with the People’s Bank of China for five years, securing a reserve backstop through the 2027 presidential election.

## Forward Market Significance

The July US employment report on Aug. 7 is the immediate test of the Treasury selloff and the Fed’s divided reaction function. Consensus calls for an 80,000 increase in nonfarm payrolls after 57,000, with unemployment unchanged at 4.2%. Hiring breadth, wages and participation must clarify whether low initial claims describe a resilient labor market or whether the rise in continuing claims is the better signal of weakening re-employment.

A firm report would reinforce Musalem’s preference for meaningful restraint and increase the relevance of Daly’s broadening-inflation scenario. A weak result would give the Fed more reason to wait, especially after Q2 productivity exceeded expectations and unit labor costs rose less than forecast. The following inflation data must then be judged against Musalem’s indication that monthly readings slightly below 0.2% would support a return toward 2%.

Hormuz requires operational access rather than another diplomatic milestone. The key questions are which vessels may use the proposed route, whether the US and other excluded parties accept the arrangement, whether insurers treat passage as safe and whether attacks spread to alternative corridors. A route that restores sustained commercial traffic would reduce the energy contribution to breakevens; restrictions, compensation demands or renewed attacks would preserve the inflation premium.

Alphabet’s new bonds provide the next test of capacity for AI financing. Secondary trading will show whether the 130-basis-point spread on the longest tranche and the broader concessions were enough to support the deal after its large orderbook was allocated. Stability in both the new securities and Alphabet’s February bonds would distinguish price-sensitive demand from temporary order inflation. Further widening would strengthen the case that recurring hyperscaler supply is absorbing more balance-sheet capacity even when primary transactions clear.

Japan’s September policy expectations remain tied to both domestic inflation and the yen. The 30-year auction showed that yields near 4% can attract demand, but its wider tail and concentrated allocation stopped short of proving broad sponsorship for super-long debt. The next currency intervention would also reveal whether Japan continues to avoid FIMA, draws on foreign official cash pools or begins using the Fed backstop it has said may be part of future operations.

The global tightening tests remain country-specific. Russia’s September meeting must determine whether the central bank validates its assumption that fuel pressure is temporary despite higher inflation forecasts and political demands for lower rates. The Philippines’ Aug. 27 decision will test whether another increase pushes the 10-year yield toward the area where strategists expect stronger demand. In India, the autumn consumption season and the next core-inflation readings will determine whether the shift of the expected first hike to December can persist.

Fed data showed no use of the FIMA repo facility during Japan’s recent currency operations, resolving one concern about the funding route without identifying the alternative. Higher domestic yields are also drawing new corporate issuers while investors demand stronger covenants.

section_summaries.section_title: Inflation Risk Keeps Global Policy Paths Divergent
section_summaries.summary: Persistent inflation kept policy paths country-specific. Banxico held at 6.50% and delayed its expected return to target, while Colombia’s internal debate remained tilted toward possible tightening. Russia cut to 14% despite higher inflation forecasts and political pressure for cheaper credit; India pushed expected tightening later as core inflation stayed contained, while Philippine yields faced another possible increase and heavy supply.

The immediate tests are whether the Aug. 7 US employment report resolves the conflict between low layoffs and weaker re-employment, whether Hormuz arrangements deliver sustained commercial access, and whether Alphabet’s new bonds stabilize after allocation. These outcomes will determine whether the Treasury selloff retains support from policy, energy and financing risk.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries sell off as a restricted Hormuz plan revives oil risk and Fed officials keep rate increases in view
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasury yields rose across maturities after emerging terms of an Iran-Oman shipping plan suggested that passage through the Strait of Hormuz could remain restricted for US, Israeli and other vessels. WTI gained 3.80% to $78.08, helping lift the 10-year breakeven 3.1 basis points to 2.249%, while the 10-year real yield rose 3.5 basis points to 2.432%. The nominal 10-year yield increased 6.6 basis points to 4.681%, and similar moves at 2 and 10 years left the 2s10s curve unchanged at 43.2 basis points.

US data offered reasons for patience but did not settle the policy outlook. Productivity exceeded expectations and unit labor costs undershot consensus, while low initial claims contrasted with higher continuing claims. Fed officials nevertheless emphasized the risk that tariffs, energy costs and AI investment could broaden inflation, and Chair Kevin Warsh was reported to be prepared to raise rates in September if inflation runs hot.

Credit remained available but increasingly price-sensitive. Alphabet placed $25 billion of bonds after attracting about $115 billion of peak orders, yet paid larger concessions as investors assessed recurring AI-related supply. Cross-markets showed pressure rather than disorder, with modest equity declines, a firmer dollar and lower volatility.
